Title: How do YOU sort your cards?

Messages.Author: Sudden Reversal
Messages.Body:
We all have them, we all need them, but how the hell do you find them when you need to?

Are your cards just shoved in a shoebox or are they lovingly entombed in alphabetical order within an oaken casket?

How much time is taken when deck building is actually fishing out the cards and what can we do to minimise the time taken to merge broken down decks back into the fold?

Do players find inventory tools like in FELD and ARDB useful and worth the time to input. If so, which is the better of the two for robustness and ease of use?

What is the most efficient way to order and organise our cards?

And the burning question for my own collection, what to do with those pesky multi-discipline cards that don't seem to fit anywhere?!

Feel free to attach glorious photographic example of your efficiency or lack thereof.

Aaron
Archbishop
Adelaide

Messages.Author: Amenophobis
Messages.Body:
I have big binders for my complete collection.

Vampires are sorted by sect/clan, grouping and capacity.

Library cards by type and/or special trait (masters: discipline, locations, archteype, trophy, out-of-turn, etc.) or discipline or clan.

One binder for each type of card (sometimes 2 or 3).

pckvtes.wordpress.com

Messages.Author: Pendargon
Messages.Body:
My vampires are sorted by clans, i find that enough

My cards are sorted by disciplines, and within that by type (action/reaction/modifier/combat...)

My masters are biggest problems, as they are sorted in groups only understandable to me like this : clan masters / master disciplines/ rarely used masters/ often used masters

Multidiscipline cards go with the discipline where they "feel " more at home (for instance, scalpel tongue goes with presence, and mind of the wilds with animalism and so on...)

To take all cards out and sleeve them into a deck - around 15 minutes.

As for deckbuilding tools i do not use them. i prefer pen-and-paper, though i do use FELDB to remind me of some cards i may have missed off the top of my head

Messages.Author: Jeff Kuta
Messages.Body:
I have 3-4 slot boxes sorted by set with multiple sets in each box. Sets are separated into vampires (sorted by clan, then capacity largest to smallest) and library cards (by rarity, then type [Masters and Events, non clan first, then clan. Library cards--Action, Equip, Politics, Retainer, Ally, ActMod, Reax, Combat, Combo...no requirements first, then clans, then disciplines, then alphabetical).

I have a single large 4-slot "play" box filled with the cards I use uncommonly. I also have two single slot boxes, one generic, one specific to Assamite disciplines and clan cards, which have the cards I use most commonly of all.

This way I don't have to go through the depths of my collection too often and makes it easier to find what I need.

I also have a couple boxes dedicated to my set collections. Those remain untouched unless I need something specific for a tournament.

Messages.Author: KevinM
Messages.Body:
If you exclusively use a computer tool like ARDB or FELDB to build your decks, the most efficient way to sort cards is:

Library A-Z (six 5000ct boxes, in my collection)
Crypt A-Z (two 5000ct boxes, in my collection)

I never, ever hold stacks of cards and look at them anymore. Nor do I look at all my "[card type]" and think how I could use these cards. Since I'm doing all that on the computer and I never build a RL deck without having testing it online for several games and having dozens of friends comment on it, Library A-Z and Crypt A-Z is the way to go. No other sub-sort is relevant.

Messages.Author: Lönkka
Messages.Body:
I store my cards in  2400 count boxes . Used shoeboxes and such for ages but got tired on non-standard sized boxes and setteled for boxes that were designed for CCGs. Sure they cost a couple euros but are SO much easier to use and store.

Library cards:
When Nights of Reckoning came out I separated all cards that don't require a vampire from the rest. Not that sure if it was that hot a move, but it has been useful sometimes when I've built a deck that focuses heavily on Allies.

Otherwise library cards are organized by:
-cards not requiring anything (within: by cardtype)
-cards requiring a discipline (within: by cardtype but combos first and multi-discipline cards are considered to be a separate discipline "AA")
-cards requiring a clan (-"-)
-cards requiring a sect (-"-)

If a card benefits, say a clan, then those are thrown in with the cards that require the same clan. For example Siphon, certain Crusades/Paxis Seizures etc.

Crypt cards are organized by clan and then alphabetically.
(I have binders that contain the latest version of each card and in those vampires are organized by group within their clan)

Ah, I see little benefit in involving rarity to the mix.
Used to do so, but gave it up.
Doesn't help deck building...

Messages.Author: Chaitan
Messages.Body:
I have Three large plastic boxes, two smaller and a two plastic row and all cards in piles separated by cardboards.

First box has piles of vampires sorted by clan+clan cards, capacity and group.

Second box has discipline cards each pile is one discipline in chaotic order.

Third box is misc cards, one pile for master discipline cards, two piles for non-discipline action cards, two piles for vote cards, one pile for non-discipline reaction cards, one pile for non-discipline combat cards, one pile for weapons, one pile for non-weapon equipment, one pile for event cards, one pile for tri-discipline cards, one pile for anarch cards, one pile for black hand cards and so on.

Then I have two smaller boxes for cards I never use or have too many of.

A plastic top that fits into one of the smaller boxes hold that has two rows of master cards sorted by alphabet.
Another plastic top with two rows hold all bloodline specific cards (vampires, disciplines, others).

I'm planning to buy five www.bcwsupplies.com/products/trading-card-boxes/super-monster-storage-box-5000-ct.htm with dividers and sort all cards (roughly ~24000) by alphabet but I need to motivate me to that the huge transport cost to Sweden is worth it just for some pieces of cardboard.

[edit]
I have another small box for finished decks. I have about 30-40 decks and construct/de-construct about 1-2 per week.

Oh and then the final file/pile is unsorted cards and decks either in the making or currently being modified/disassembled.

Messages.Author: LunaSlave
Messages.Body:
It's sort of a confusing system to explain, but it works well for me. The idea behind it was to be organized enough that I could build decks using ARDB but not have to rely on it - and that I could use this system to just grab a handful of cards from the sections I want in order to build a deck quickly by browsing through the cards and seeing what I find interesting.

A few boxes containing all of my decks

vampires are sorted by sect - meaning each clan is put with the sect it is nominally in (Gangrel go with Camarilla, not independent) and then by clan within that, and then alphabetically within that.

Library cards in alphabetical order in the following groups (and by generic I mean that it doesn't require or predominantly favor a clan, sect or discipline)

Event
Generic combat/action/action mod/reaction cards
Generic allies
Generic retainers
Generic masters
Master: Discipline
Generic Equipment cards
Generic political cards
Clan-requiring cards (non-bloodlines, sorted by clan)
Discipline requiring cards (non-bloodlines, sorted by discipline)
Pseudo-discipline stuff
Multi-discipline requiring stuff (non-bloodline)

Sect-requiring or helping cards (ie stuff for Anarch, Black Hand, Cam, Laibon, Sabbat, each with their own category)

various Imbued junk

a section for each bloodline Discipline (sorted by bloodlines discipline, no regard to outferior) and flight
Bloodlines clan-specific stuff

all Bloodlines related library cards get their own box for convenience.
and finally, all Jyhad-backed cards get their own box, cause i like to sometimes build all Jyhad-backed decks just for nostalgia's sake.
